title: Indian Army Opens Dhurandhar-Themed Bar at Srinagar Mess, Blending Bollywood and Military Culture
excerpt: An Army mess in Srinagar has inaugurated a bar themed around the blockbuster Dhurandhar films, with actor Rakesh Bedi cutting the ribbon and showcasing artwork of Ranveer Singh and R. Madhavan.
body:
• An Army mess in Srinagar has opened a 'Dhurandhar bar' themed around the Ranveer Singh spy franchise directed by Aditya Dhar
  • Actor Rakesh Bedi, who appeared in both films, inaugurated the bar and shared a video tour on Instagram Stories
  • The bar features film posters, artwork of Ranveer Singh with a real gun incorporated into the display, and motifs from the cast
  • The Dhurandhar franchise has grossed over ₹3,100 crore worldwide across both installments

A military mess in Srinagar has inaugurated what it calls the 'Dhurandhar bar' — a themed space built around Aditya Dhar's blockbuster spy franchise starring Ranveer Singh. The bar, complete with film posters, character artwork, and military-meets-cinema decor, was opened by actor Rakesh Bedi, who featured in both Dhurandhar films.

Bedi shared a video tour of the bar on Instagram Stories on Friday, noting he had been invited to cut the ribbon. "I am in Srinagar. I won't go into details of where I am, but this is an Army mess," he said, citing security constraints. "Here, they have made a Dhurandhar corner. They were waiting for someone to come and inaugurate it."

Inside the Dhurandhar Bar

The space greets visitors with a sign reading 'Dhurandhar bar, established 2026.' A poster of actor Gaurav Gera, who played a milk soda seller in the film, shows him mixing a drink alongside a catchphrase from his character. Another poster features Bedi himself with a drink-themed line from his role.

The centerpiece is an artwork of Ranveer Singh's character that creatively incorporates a real gun to enhance the visual effect — a fitting touch for a military setting. A separate piece features R. Madhavan, who portrayed India's National Security Advisor in the franchise. Bedi did not disclose the exact location of the bar within Srinagar for security reasons.

"I happened to be here in Kashmir, in Srinagar, and I am going to do the honours. I am honoured to do that."

— Rakesh Bedi, Actor

A Box Office Phenomenon

The Dhurandhar franchise, directed by Aditya Dhar, has been one of Indian cinema's biggest commercial successes. The original film, released in December 2025, follows Jaskirat Singh Rangi — played by Ranveer Singh — an Indian spy who infiltrates a Karachi gang led by Rehman Dakait, portrayed by Akshaye Khanna. The story centers on dismantling an ISI-supported terror network in Pakistan.

The first film grossed ₹1,300 crore worldwide. Its sequel, Dhurandhar: The Revenge, released in March 2026, surpassed expectations with over ₹1,800 crore in global earnings, making the franchise one of the highest-grossing in Indian cinema history. The sequel featured a more restrained performance from Singh, earning praise from critics. Livemint's review noted that "the restraint is not the absence of emotion — it is the accumulation of it."

When Bollywood Meets the Barracks

The Dhurandhar bar is an unusual example of popular cinema permeating military culture. While Bollywood films with patriotic and military themes — from Border to Uri: The Surgical Strike — have long resonated with armed forces personnel, the creation of a dedicated themed space within an Army mess represents a newer form of cultural crossover.

The franchise's focus on covert operations, Kashmir, and India-Pakistan dynamics gives it particular resonance in Srinagar, where the Army maintains a significant presence. The films also feature Sara Arjun and Arjun Rampal in notable supporting roles.

As the Dhurandhar franchise continues to shape pop culture months after release, the Srinagar bar stands as evidence that its influence extends well beyond the multiplex — into the messes where soldiers unwind after duty.
